```{r}
#| label: setup

# Introduction
#
# Reports the headline numbers and draws Figure 1 (map and tree sizes) and
# Figure 2 (most frequent non-baobab species) to the Nature Portfolio figure
# specifications used by Scientific Data, plus a map for the project web page.


# Packages

required_packages <- c("readr", "dplyr", "tidyr", "stringr", "forcats", "ggplot2",
                       "patchwork","scales", "sf", "rnaturalearth",
                       "rnaturalearthdata", "knitr",
                       "ragg", "systemfonts")
missing_packages <- required_packages[!vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace,
                                              logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop("Please install these packages first: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "),
       call. = FALSE)
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(stringr)
  library(forcats)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(patchwork)
  library(sf)
})

# Figure settings (Nature Portfolio guide): widths of 89 or 183 mm, height of
# at most 170 mm, Arial or Helvetica text of 5-7 pt, 8 pt bold panel labels,
# lines of 0.25-1 pt.

single_column_mm   <- 89
double_column_mm   <- 183
maximum_height_mm  <- 170
figure_1_height_mm <- 135
figure_2_height_mm <- 85
webpage_map_size_mm <- 210   
figure_resolution_dpi <- 600
text_size_pt        <- 7
small_text_size_pt  <- 6
panel_label_size_pt <- 8
thin_line_pt     <- 0.25
standard_line_pt <- 0.5
line_width <- function(points) points / (ggplot2::.pt * 72 / 96)  # points to ggplot2 linewidth
choose_figure_font <- function() {
  preferred_fonts <- c("Arial", "Helvetica", "Liberation Sans", "Arimo")
  installed_fonts <- unique(systemfonts::system_fonts()$family)
  available <- intersect(preferred_fonts, installed_fonts)
  if (length(available) == 0) {
    warning("Neither Arial nor Helvetica is installed; the default sans-serif font is used.",
            call. = FALSE)
    return("sans")
  }
  available[1]
}
figure_font <- choose_figure_font()
# Blue and orange remain distinct under common colour-vision deficiencies.
tree_type_colours <- c("baobab" = "#2a78d6", "non-baobab" = "#eb6834", "not recorded" = "#8c8c8c")
tree_type_labels  <- c("baobab" = "Baobab", "non-baobab" = "Non-baobab", "not recorded" = "Not recorded")

number_of_species_shown <- 15

```

```{r}
#| label: read-data

# pipeline_paths.csv is written by step 1 in the folder of this document.
if (!file.exists("pipeline_paths.csv")) {
  stop("pipeline_paths.csv was not found next to this document. Run Harmonise_tree_data.R first.",
       call. = FALSE)
}
pipeline_paths <- read_csv("pipeline_paths.csv", col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                           na = character(), progress = FALSE)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(pipeline_paths))) assign(pipeline_paths$name[i], pipeline_paths$value[i])

# Variables are used by dictionary role, so they can be renamed in the
# dictionary.

dictionary_roles <- read_csv(dictionary_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                             progress = FALSE)[, c("variable_name", "role")]
rename_to_roles <- function(table) {
  hit <- names(table) %in% dictionary_roles$variable_name
  names(table)[hit] <- dictionary_roles$role[match(names(table)[hit], dictionary_roles$variable_name)]
  table
}
if (!identical(params$public_data_file, "")) public_data_file <- params$public_data_file
if (!identical(params$figures_folder, ""))   figures_folder   <- params$figures_folder
if (!file.exists(public_data_file)) {
  stop("The public data file was not found: ", public_data_file,
       ". Run QAQC_BAM_Data.qmd first.", call. = FALSE)
}


# Every value is read as text so that nothing changes on reading.
public_data <- read_csv(public_data_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                        na = c("", "NA"), progress = FALSE) %>% rename_to_roles()

required_variables <- c("record_id", "tree_type", "latitude", "longitude", "country", "date",
                        "observer_name", "circumference", "height", "crown_1", "crown_2",
                        "accepted_species_name")
missing_variables <- setdiff(required_variables, names(public_data))
if (length(missing_variables) > 0) {
  stop("These variables are missing from the public dataset: ",
       paste(missing_variables, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}

dir.create(figures_folder, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Girth is converted to metres; canopy area is an ellipse from the two
# perpendicular crown diameters.
tree_data <- public_data %>%
  transmute(
    record_id,
    tree_type      = factor(coalesce(tree_type, "not recorded"), levels = names(tree_type_colours)),
    latitude       = as.numeric(latitude),
    longitude      = as.numeric(longitude),
    country,
    year           = as.integer(str_sub(date, 1, 4)),
    girth_m        = as.numeric(circumference) / 100,
    height_m       = as.numeric(height),
    crown_ns_m     = as.numeric(crown_1),
    crown_ew_m     = as.numeric(crown_2),
    canopy_area_m2 = pi * (crown_ns_m / 2) * (crown_ew_m / 2),
    accepted_species_name, observer_name
  )

typed_trees <- filter(tree_data, tree_type != "not recorded") %>% mutate(tree_type = droplevels(tree_type))
```

```{r}
#| label: theme-and-helpers

theme_publication <- function() {
  theme_classic(base_size = text_size_pt, base_family = figure_font,
                base_line_size = line_width(standard_line_pt),
                base_rect_size = line_width(standard_line_pt)) +
    theme(
      text               = element_text(colour = "black"),
      axis.title         = element_text(size = text_size_pt, colour = "black"),
      axis.text          = element_text(size = small_text_size_pt, colour = "black"),
      axis.line          = element_line(linewidth = line_width(standard_line_pt), colour = "black"),
      axis.ticks         = element_line(linewidth = line_width(standard_line_pt), colour = "black"),
      axis.ticks.length  = unit(1, "mm"),
      panel.grid         = element_blank(),
      legend.position    = "bottom",
      legend.title       = element_text(size = text_size_pt, colour = "black"),
      legend.text        = element_text(size = small_text_size_pt, colour = "black"),
      legend.key.size    = unit(3, "mm"),
      legend.margin      = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
      plot.tag           = element_text(size = panel_label_size_pt, face = "bold", colour = "black"),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = small_text_size_pt, colour = "black",
                                        margin = margin(b = 1.5, unit = "mm")),
      plot.margin        = margin(2, 3, 2, 2, unit = "mm"),
      strip.background   = element_blank()
    )
}


legend_tree_types <- c("baobab", "non-baobab")
scale_tree_colour <- scale_colour_manual(values = tree_type_colours, labels = tree_type_labels[legend_tree_types],
                                         breaks = legend_tree_types, name = "Tree type", drop = TRUE)
scale_tree_fill   <- scale_fill_manual(values = tree_type_colours, labels = tree_type_labels[legend_tree_types],
                                       breaks = legend_tree_types, name = "Tree type", drop = TRUE)


sample_size_label <- function(data, ...) {
  counts <- data %>%
    filter(if_all(c(...), ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
    count(tree_type)
  paste0("n = ", paste(format(counts$n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), str_to_lower(tree_type_labels[as.character(counts$tree_type)]),
                       collapse = "; "))
}

add_sample_size <- function(label) {
  labs(subtitle = label)
}


describe_distribution <- function(values, unit, digits = 1) {
  values <- values[!is.na(values)]
  quartiles <- quantile(values, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f %s (IQR %.", digits, "f\u2013%.", digits, "f %s)"),
          quartiles[2], unit, quartiles[1], quartiles[3], unit)
}


save_journal_figure <- function(figure, file_stem, width_mm, height_mm) {
  if (height_mm > maximum_height_mm) {
    warning(file_stem, " is taller than ", maximum_height_mm, " mm.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  ggsave(file.path(figures_folder, paste0(file_stem, ".pdf")), figure,
         width = width_mm, height = height_mm, units = "mm", bg = "white",
         device = cairo_pdf)
  ggsave(file.path(figures_folder, paste0(file_stem, ".png")), figure,
         width = width_mm, height = height_mm, units = "mm", bg = "white",
         dpi = figure_resolution_dpi, device = ragg::agg_png)
}

# Panel labels
panel_tags <- plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
```

```{r}
#| label: summary-numbers

number_of_records   <- nrow(tree_data)
number_of_baobabs   <- sum(tree_data$tree_type == "baobab")
number_of_others    <- sum(tree_data$tree_type == "non-baobab")
number_untyped      <- sum(tree_data$tree_type == "not recorded")
country_names       <- sort(unique(na.omit(tree_data$country)))


# The number of contributed datasets comes from step 3, as source files are
# not published.
manuscript_numbers_file <- file.path(qaqc_results_folder, "manuscript_numbers.csv")
number_of_datasets <- NA_integer_
if (file.exists(manuscript_numbers_file)) {
  manuscript_numbers <- read_csv(manuscript_numbers_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                                 progress = FALSE)
  number_of_datasets <- as.integer(manuscript_numbers$value[manuscript_numbers$quantity == "Source files"][1])
}

# "Anonymous" is not a person and is not counted among named observers.
named_observers <- tree_data$observer_name %>%
  na.omit() %>%
  str_split("\\s*;\\s*") %>%
  unlist() %>%
  str_squish() %>%
  setdiff(c("", "Anonymous")) %>%
  sort()

survey_years <- sort(unique(na.omit(tree_data$year)))

country_ranking   <- sort(table(tree_data$country), decreasing = TRUE)
top_two_countries <- names(country_ranking)[1:2]
top_two_share     <- round(100 * sum(country_ranking[1:2]) / number_of_records, 1)

format_count <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
```

# Overview

This report summarises the public dataset of the *Baobabs in Africa Mapped (BAM) Project*, produced after harmonisation and quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC). The dataset contains `r format_count(number_of_records)` tree observations: `r format_count(number_of_baobabs)` baobabs (*Adansonia digitata*), `r format_count(number_of_others)` non-baobab trees and `r format_count(number_untyped)` trees whose type was not recorded. The observations come from `r if (is.na(number_of_datasets)) "several" else number_of_datasets` contributed datasets, cover `r length(country_names)` countries (`r paste(country_names, collapse = ", ")`) and were made between `r min(survey_years)` and `r max(survey_years)`. `r length(named_observers)` observers agreed to be named publicly.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the public dataset."
knitr::kable(tibble(
  Measure = c("Tree observations", "Baobab observations", "Non-baobab observations"
              ,"Tree type not recorded", "Countries", "Contributed datasets",
              "Survey years", "Observers named with consent"),
  Value = c(format_count(c(number_of_records, number_of_baobabs, number_of_others, number_untyped,
                           length(country_names))),
            if (is.na(number_of_datasets)) "not available" else format_count(number_of_datasets),
            paste(min(survey_years), "to", max(survey_years)),
            format_count(length(named_observers)))
), format = "pipe", align = "lr")
```

# Distribution and size of the trees

@fig-distribution-size shows where the trees were recorded and how their size differs between baobabs and non-baobab trees. The two best-represented countries, `r top_two_countries[1]` and `r top_two_countries[2]`, together account for `r format_count(sum(country_ranking[1:2]))` records (`r top_two_share`%). Baobabs have a median stem girth of `r describe_distribution(typed_trees$girth_m[typed_trees$tree_type == "baobab"], "m", 2)`, compared with `r describe_distribution(typed_trees$girth_m[typed_trees$tree_type == "non-baobab"], "m", 2)` for non-baobab trees. Median heights are `r describe_distribution(typed_trees$height_m[typed_trees$tree_type == "baobab"], "m")` for baobabs and `r describe_distribution(typed_trees$height_m[typed_trees$tree_type == "non-baobab"], "m")` for non-baobab trees, and median canopy areas are `r describe_distribution(typed_trees$canopy_area_m2[typed_trees$tree_type == "baobab"], "m\u00b2", 0)` and `r describe_distribution(typed_trees$canopy_area_m2[typed_trees$tree_type == "non-baobab"], "m\u00b2", 0)` respectively.

```{r}
#| label: fig-distribution-size
#| fig-cap: "Distribution and size of baobab and non-baobab trees in the BAM public dataset. **a**, Locations of tree observations, coloured by tree type; grey points are trees whose type was not recorded. **b**–**d**, Probability density of stem girth (**b**), tree height (**c**) and canopy area (**d**); canopy area is calculated as an ellipse from the two perpendicular crown diameters. Girth and canopy area are shown on logarithmic axes. n gives the number of trees in each panel; trees whose type was not recorded are not shown in **b**–**d**."
#| fig-width: 7.205
#| fig-height: 5.315
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-pos: "htbp"


sf_use_s2(FALSE)  # planar operations are sufficient for drawing
world_countries <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
map_countries   <- filter(world_countries, continent == "Africa")

tree_points <- tree_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) %>%
  arrange(tree_type == "non-baobab") %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

# The map frame is mainland Africa and Madagascar; small outlying islands do
# not set it. It widens only if a tree lies outside.
minimum_land_area_sq_degrees <- 1
africa_land_parts <- st_cast(st_geometry(map_countries), "POLYGON")
land_part_area    <- as.numeric(st_area(st_set_crs(africa_land_parts, NA)))
africa_main_land  <- africa_land_parts[land_part_area >= minimum_land_area_sq_degrees]
africa_frame      <- st_bbox(africa_main_land)

points_frame       <- st_bbox(tree_points)
map_margin_degrees <- 2
map_extent <- c(xmin = min(africa_frame[["xmin"]], points_frame[["xmin"]]) - map_margin_degrees,
                xmax = max(africa_frame[["xmax"]], points_frame[["xmax"]]) + map_margin_degrees,
                ymin = min(africa_frame[["ymin"]], points_frame[["ymin"]]) - map_margin_degrees,
                ymax = max(africa_frame[["ymax"]], points_frame[["ymax"]]) + map_margin_degrees)

# Coordinates are written as plain text so the degree sign prints on every
# system.
format_longitude <- function(degrees) {
  paste0(abs(degrees), "\u00b0", ifelse(degrees > 0, "E", ifelse(degrees < 0, "W", "")))
}
format_latitude <- function(degrees) {
  paste0(abs(degrees), "\u00b0", ifelse(degrees > 0, "N", ifelse(degrees < 0, "S", "")))
}

panel_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = world_countries, fill = "white", colour = "grey75", linewidth = line_width(thin_line_pt)) +
  geom_sf(data = map_countries, fill = "grey92", colour = "grey55", linewidth = line_width(thin_line_pt)) +
  geom_sf(data = tree_points, aes(fill = tree_type), shape = 21, colour = "white",
          stroke = line_width(thin_line_pt) / 2, size = 1.1, alpha = 0.85) +
  coord_sf(xlim = unname(map_extent[c("xmin", "xmax")]), ylim = unname(map_extent[c("ymin", "ymax")]),
           expand = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-20, 60, by = 20), labels = format_longitude) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-30, 30, by = 15), labels = format_latitude) +
  scale_tree_fill +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_publication() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#eef3f8", colour = NA),
        axis.line = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = line_width(standard_line_pt)))

density_panel <- function(variable, x_label, log_scale = FALSE) {
  panel <- ggplot(filter(typed_trees, !is.na(.data[[variable]])),
                  aes(x = .data[[variable]], fill = tree_type, colour = tree_type)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = line_width(0.75), adjust = 1) +
    add_sample_size(sample_size_label(typed_trees, all_of(variable))) +
    scale_tree_fill + scale_tree_colour +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = "Probability density") +
    theme_publication()
  if (log_scale) {
    panel <- panel + scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE, big.mark = ","))
  }
  panel
}

panel_girth_density  <- density_panel("girth_m", "Stem girth (m)", log_scale = TRUE)
panel_height_density <- density_panel("height_m", "Tree height (m)")
canopy_axis_label    <- expression("Canopy area (m"^2*")")
panel_canopy_density <- density_panel("canopy_area_m2", canopy_axis_label, log_scale = TRUE)

no_legend <- guides(fill = "none", colour = "none")
panel_girth_density  <- panel_girth_density  + no_legend
panel_height_density <- panel_height_density + no_legend
panel_canopy_density <- panel_canopy_density + no_legend

# The map fills the left of the figure; the density panels are stacked on the
# right. Brackets are needed because | binds less tightly than +.
figure_distribution_size <- (panel_map |
  (panel_girth_density / panel_height_density / panel_canopy_density)) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(2.1, 1), guides = "collect") +
  panel_tags &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

save_journal_figure(figure_distribution_size, "figure_1_distribution_and_size",
                    width_mm = double_column_mm, height_mm = figure_1_height_mm)
figure_distribution_size
```

# Species composition

```{r}
#| label: species-numbers

non_baobabs <- filter(typed_trees, tree_type == "non-baobab")
if (all(is.na(non_baobabs$accepted_species_name))) {
  stop("No non-baobab tree has an accepted species name. Set wfo_backbone_file in ",
       "Harmonise_tree_data.R and render QAQC_BAM_Data.qmd again.", call. = FALSE)
}

species_counts <- non_baobabs %>%
  filter(!is.na(accepted_species_name)) %>%
  count(accepted_species_name, name = "records") %>%
  rename(name = accepted_species_name) %>%
  arrange(desc(records))

species_shown <- head(species_counts, number_of_species_shown)

non_baobabs_without_name <- sum(is.na(non_baobabs$accepted_species_name))
```

@fig-species shows the `r number_of_species_shown` most frequently recorded non-baobab species. Species are shown by their accepted names in the World Flora Online (WFO) taxonomic backbone; `r format_count(non_baobabs_without_name)` non-baobab trees have no accepted species name (no species recorded, or a name that could not be matched exactly at species level) and are not shown.

```{r}
#| label: fig-species
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("The ", number_of_species_shown, " most frequently recorded non-baobab species in the BAM public dataset, by accepted name in World Flora Online.")
#| fig-width: 3.504
#| fig-height: 3.346
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-pos: "htbp"

figure_species <- ggplot(species_shown, aes(x = records, y = fct_reorder(name, records))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, fill = tree_type_colours[["non-baobab"]]) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma(),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +  # Bars start at zero.
  labs(x = "Number of non-baobab trees", y = NULL) +
  theme_publication() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank())

save_journal_figure(figure_species, "figure_2_species",
                    width_mm = single_column_mm, height_mm = figure_2_height_mm)
figure_species
```

```{r}
#| label: environment-data

# Reads the outputs of Environmental_covariates.R so that the figure and the
# numbers quoted beside it come from the same run.

# PDF keeps the figure as vector graphics in the PDF report; PNG is used for
# Word or HTML output.
environment_figure_extension <- if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "pdf" else "png"

# File names written by Environmental_covariates.R (Section 11 and Section 12).
environment_figure_file <- file.path(figures_folder,
                                     paste0("figure_3_environment.", environment_figure_extension))
covariates_file <- file.path(environment_results_folder, "baobab_environmental_covariates.csv")

# The report stops with a clear message if step 5 has not been run.
for (needed_file in c(covariates_file, environment_figure_file)) {
  if (!file.exists(needed_file)) {
    stop(basename(needed_file), " was not found. Run Environmental_covariates.R ",
         "before rendering this report.", call. = FALSE)
  }
}

# Covariates older than the public file were extracted from an earlier
# version of the data.
if (file.mtime(covariates_file) < file.mtime(public_data_file)) {
  warning("The environmental covariates are older than the public data file; ",
          "run Environmental_covariates.R again.", call. = FALSE)
}

# One row per unique baobab location.
covariates <- read_csv(covariates_file, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)

number_of_locations <- nrow(covariates)
semi_arid_share     <- round(100 * mean(covariates$aridity_class == "Semi-arid", na.rm = TRUE))
protected_share     <- round(100 * mean(covariates$in_protected_area, na.rm = TRUE))

# The aridity index has no unit, so it is written without one.
aridity_quartiles <- quantile(covariates$aridity_index, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
aridity_text <- sprintf("%.2f (IQR %.2f–%.2f)", aridity_quartiles[2], aridity_quartiles[1],
                        aridity_quartiles[3])
```

# Environment of the baobab locations

@fig-environment describes the environment at the `r format_count(number_of_locations)` unique baobab locations. Mean annual precipitation has a median of `r describe_distribution(covariates$precipitation_mm, "mm", 0)` and mean annual temperature a median of `r describe_distribution(covariates$temperature_c, "°C")`. The median aridity index is `r aridity_text`, and `r semi_arid_share`% of locations fall in the semi-arid class. `r protected_share`% of locations lie inside a protected area.

```{r}
#| label: fig-environment

# Completeness of the variables

```{r}
#| label: completeness-data

# Reads the completeness of each public variable, written by QAQC_BAM_Data.qmd
# (step 3), so that the figure always matches Table 1 of the manuscript.
variable_summary_file <- file.path(qaqc_results_folder, "qaqc_variable_summary.csv")
if (!file.exists(variable_summary_file)) {
  stop("qaqc_variable_summary.csv was not found. Render QAQC_BAM_Data.qmd before this report.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

completeness_bar_colour       <- "grey60"
completeness_figure_width_mm  <- 120   # Nature Portfolio 1.5-column width
completeness_figure_height_mm <- 130
well_recorded_percent         <- 75    # threshold quoted in the text

# One row per variable in the public file, named exactly as in the file.
completeness <- read_csv(variable_summary_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                         progress = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(variable_name, percent_complete = as.numeric(percent_complete))

# format_percent() writes a percentage as a whole number, but never rounds a
# variable with a few values down to 0% or a nearly complete one up to 100%.
format_percent <- function(percent) {
  case_when(percent > 0 & percent < 1    ~ "<1%",
            percent > 99 & percent < 100 ~ ">99%",
            TRUE                         ~ paste0(round(percent), "%"))
}

number_well_recorded <- sum(completeness$percent_complete >= well_recorded_percent)
empty_variables      <- completeness$variable_name[completeness$percent_complete == 0]
```

@fig-completeness shows the percentage of the `r format_count(number_of_records)` public records that hold a value for each of the `r nrow(completeness)` variables in the public file. `r number_well_recorded` variables are recorded for at least `r well_recorded_percent`% of records.`r if (length(empty_variables) > 0) paste0(" ", paste0("\x60", empty_variables, "\x60", collapse = ", "), if (length(empty_variables) == 1) " has" else " have", " no values.") else ""`

```{r}
#| label: fig-completeness
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Completeness of the variables in the BAM public dataset, as the percentage of the ", format_count(number_of_records), " records with a value for each variable. Variables are named as in the public file and ordered from most to least complete.")'
#| fig-width: 4.724
#| fig-height: 5.118
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-pos: "htbp"

figure_completeness <- ggplot(completeness,
                              aes(x = percent_complete, y = fct_reorder(variable_name, percent_complete))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, fill = completeness_bar_colour) +
  # Percentages are written just beyond the end of each bar.
  geom_text(aes(label = format_percent(percent_complete)), hjust = -0.15,
            size = small_text_size_pt / ggplot2::.pt, family = figure_font, colour = "black") +
  # The axis runs from 0% to 100%; bars start at zero.
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 25),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
  # Labels of bars near 100% may extend past the panel, so they are not clipped.
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = "Records with a value", y = NULL) +
  theme_publication() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(2, 8, 2, 2, unit = "mm"))

save_journal_figure(figure_completeness, "figure_variable_completeness",
                    width_mm = completeness_figure_width_mm, height_mm = completeness_figure_height_mm)
figure_completeness
```

# Supplementary information

```{r}
#| label: try-data

# Reads the outputs of TRY_comparison_check.R (step 2), so that the figure and
# the numbers quoted beside it come from the same run.

# PDF keeps the figure as vector graphics in the PDF report; PNG is used for
# Word or HTML output.
try_figure_extension <- if (knitr::is_latex_output()) "pdf" else "png"

# File names written by TRY_comparison_check.R (Sections 9 and 10).
try_figure_file    <- file.path(figures_folder,
                                paste0("supplementary_figure_1_try_locations.", try_figure_extension))
try_summary_file   <- file.path(try_results_folder, "try_cross_check_summary.csv")
try_duplicate_file <- file.path(try_results_folder, "try_bam_duplicate_check.csv")

# The report stops with a clear message if step 2 has not been run.
for (needed_file in c(try_figure_file, try_summary_file, try_duplicate_file)) {
  if (!file.exists(needed_file)) {
    stop(basename(needed_file), " was not found. Run TRY_comparison_check.R ",
         "before rendering this report.", call. = FALSE)
  }
}

# A comparison older than the harmonised dataset was made with an earlier
# version of the data.
if (file.mtime(try_summary_file) < file.mtime(harmonised_dataset_file)) {
  warning("The TRY comparison is older than the harmonised dataset; ",
          "run TRY_comparison_check.R again.", call. = FALSE)
}

# One row per measure, with its value as text.
try_summary <- read_csv(try_summary_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                        progress = FALSE)

# try_value() returns the value of one measure in the summary table.
try_value <- function(measure) {
  value <- try_summary$value[try_summary$measure == measure]
  if (length(value) == 0) NA_character_ else value[1]
}

try_observations       <- try_value("TRY Adansonia observations")
try_with_coordinates   <- try_value("TRY Adansonia observations with coordinates")
try_digitata_located   <- try_value("Adansonia digitata observations with coordinates")
try_probable_duplicates <- try_value("Probable duplicates of BAM records")

# Distance from each georeferenced A. digitata observation in TRY to the
# nearest BAM baobab, in kilometres.
try_digitata_distances_km <- read_csv(try_duplicate_file, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                                      progress = FALSE) %>%
  filter(str_detect(coalesce(species, ""), fixed("Adansonia digitata")),
         !is.na(nearest_bam_distance_m)) %>%
  mutate(distance_km = round(as.numeric(nearest_bam_distance_m) / 1000)) %>%
  arrange(distance_km) %>%
  pull(distance_km)
```

Supplementary Figure 1 compares the baobab records in the harmonised BAM dataset with the observations of the genus *Adansonia* in the TRY Plant Trait Database. The TRY release held `r try_observations` *Adansonia* observations, of which `r try_with_coordinates` had coordinates, including `r try_digitata_located` of *A. digitata*. ``` r if (length(try_digitata_distances_km) > 0) paste0("The nearest BAM baobabs lay ", paste(format_count(try_digitata_distances_km), collapse = " and "), " km from the georeferenced *A. digitata* observations. ") else ""``r try_probable_duplicates ``` TRY observations were classified as probable duplicates of BAM records.

```{r}

Small red points are baobab records in the harmonised BAM dataset. Larger points are TRY *Adansonia* observations with coordinates, coloured by the result of the duplicate check: probable duplicate (within 50 m of a BAM baobab and matching it in height or contributor), possible duplicate, same site as BAM records but a different tree, or not in BAM. n gives the number of observations in each class; TRY observations outside Africa are not shown."
